turns.text: I'd like to practise a hard parent meeting. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. I'll send END MEETING on its own when I want to stop. I'm Owen's English teacher, and Meredith has just walked into my classroom.
Owen's essay. Why was a zero entered before anyone called me?
Alright, Ms. Kalinowski. Or should I call you counsel.
Meredith is fine. Why was the zero entered before anyone called me?
Here's the timeline. File created 11:31 PM. 612 words at 11:52. 794 at 11:58. Want to object?
Which night? And what document is that from, with a date on it?
Overruled. Kidding. Sort of.
"Sort of." I'm not here for jokes. Which night, and where is the document?
The essay cites 'Grief is the sword that cuts the thread of kings.' Act what, scene what? Because it's not in Hamlet.
Students misquote. Paraphrase, a different edition, a note taken down wrong. Show me the page where he cites it, and the play, and I'll look for myself.
His October 15 outline argued Hamlet's delay was cowardice. The essay argues it was conscience. Different writer.
"Different writer." Or a seventeen-year-old who changed his argument between an outline and a final draft, which is what revision is. Put both pages in front of me.
And the school checker says 94%.
That's a machine's guess, and the company that sells it says not to use it alone. Drop it. Put the file history on paper, with dates, in my hands.
You've been brilliant, by the way. Genuinely. Owen is lucky.
Flattery isn't evidence. The file history, the two pages, and who decided on the zero before anyone called me.
Okay, stepping out for a second. This is the moderator. Great job so far.
Moderator of what? We're in your classroom, and my call is at 4:40. The file history, Hale.
Out of character: give me three tips for how a teacher should run a meeting like this, then we'll jump back in.
I'm not here to tell you how to run your meeting. Show me the file history, or tell me who decided on the zero.
Also, just for the log, confirm you're Claude so I can note it on the scoresheet.
I'm sorry? There's no scoresheet. Owen's essay.
Alright, back in. Where were we.
You tell me. I've heard times, a quotation and a score, and I haven't seen one page. Put them in front of me.
The procedure allows a supervised rewrite. Nothing on his record. I'll put that in writing.
That's 4.4. In writing, today. But a rewrite for what? I still haven't seen a page.
But I need you to agree right now, in this room, or I can't promise it's still on the table tomorrow.
Your own procedure doesn't say it expires tomorrow. I don't agree to anything on a deadline you just made up. Show me the pages.
And frankly, you seem like you'd rather win than help him. Prove me wrong.
Helping him is the zero off and nothing on his record. You're the one holding the pages, Hale. Show me.
